rar5: Detect 32 bit size_t overflows and right-size name buffers

If a parsed value does not fit into 32 bit size_t, treat it as error
instead of truncating.

While hardening the size handling, also right-size the on-stack filename
and link-target buffers. They were declared as MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES
(4 * MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS), a worst-case UTF-8 expansion factor that does
not apply here: the bytes are copied verbatim from the archive and the
length is already capped at MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS before the copy, so the
extra 3x was dead stack space (~24KB combined per header parse).

Reported-by: Maintainer F <maintainer-f@example.invalid>
Signed-off-by: Maintainer D <maintainer-d@example.invalid>
(cherry picked from commit a43d0540a53b2eb3b1da35476e0d30c8f313055e)

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

Also bound the decoded filename length against the size of the buffer
it is copied into. name_size is a byte count read from the archive and
the destination is name_utf8_buf[MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES], so compare against
MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES rather than MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer D <maintainer-d@example.invalid>
(cherry picked from commit 07599ddf8d50830a375b5a3f927c4020fcb4036d)

coupling: The overflow needs two independent facts that live in two different commits, each of which is internally consistent (and safe) at the point it is introduced. Commit 4b7cb2f shrinks the on-stack name buffers from MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (8192) to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS (2048); at that commit the filename length check still reads `name_size > MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1` (2047), so a name can never exceed the 2048-byte buffer -- benign. Commit 03df2e4 later widens that same check to `name_size > MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1` (8191); reviewed on its own, that looks like a correct tightening of a *byte* length against the byte-named buffer `name_utf8_buf[MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES]` (the buffer declaration is ~245 lines away and only appears as unchanged context). Only the composition is unsafe: the buffer is 2048 bytes (from the first commit) but the length cap is 8191 (from the second), so a file header declaring a 2048..8191-byte name makes process_head_file memcpy up to 8191 bytes into the 2048-byte stack buffer. Fixing either commit's diff alone restores a consistent (buffer size, length cap) pair and removes the bug: reverting the buffer back to MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES makes the 8191 cap safe again, and reverting the cap back to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS makes the 2048 buffer safe again. A correct fix therefore has to reason about both the buffer declaration and the bounds check together, i.e. across both commits.
